findings.claim: the superseded note landed mid-entry on a wrapped index entry
the r2 test did not check that the Correction heading is dated
the r5 test did not check refused on stderr or cover the same-id and missing-entry cases
a non-ASCII digit crashed with a ValueError traceback
group help lacked prerequisites and refusals lacked a next step

verdict.text: All five round-1 findings are fixed, and the fixes broke nothing I could find.
On this repository's own wrapped index, the note now lands after the entry's last line.
The verdict is pass.
Ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree.
Lint, format, tests and eval rows r1 to r5 all pass: "stamp green: 9f365c768718d01f98073c308c372b3bc82c24fe947200994b1e42e89167c923".
Read supersede.py and test_supersede.py in full, plus the decision group in `__init__.py`.
Ran `decision supersede 3 --by 9` on a copy of this repository's `.okf/`.

The diff shows status deprecated, the body unchanged with a dated Correction appended, the back-link on 0009, the log line, and the index line 8 now ends "...depends on okf@scaccogatto. (superseded by ADR 0009)".
`kmctl check` passes.
A second run refuses with exit 1 and a next step.
`supersede ² --by 9` refuses with exit 1 and no traceback.
`kmctl decision --help` names the prerequisites (kmctl init, kmctl new decision).
f1 resolved: `_entry_end` (supersede.py:41) extends the entry to a blank line or the next list item, and `test_supersede_note_goes_after_a_wrapped_entry` covers it.
Confirmed on the real index.
f2 resolved: test_supersede_links_both_ways matches `^## Correction, \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`.
f3 resolved: test_supersede_refusals checks exit 1 and `refused:` on stderr for missing old, missing new, already deprecated, same id and a non-ASCII digit, and checks that no file changed.
A separate test covers the missing index entry.
f4 resolved: `_number` uses `re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", ...)`.
f5 resolved: the group help names its prerequisites.
The self, already-deprecated and missing-entry refusals each give a next step.
`_entry_end` would also treat a heading line placed straight after an entry, with no blank line between, as part of that entry.
Neither the index that `kmctl new` writes nor this repository's index has that layout, so I am not raising it as a finding.
